claims.claim_text: Indexed Edgar Salinger is identified at high confidence as the New Yorker documented in Japanese-language government translation work and a 1940 civic committee.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two independent archival sources name the rare exact person in New York, document Japanese-language ability and place him in 1918 and 1940 contexts before the OSS index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from a rare exact name plus aligned New York, Japanese-language and chronological evidence; the personnel jacket has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both sources predate OSS, but neither states the OSS appointment date or immediate predecessor employer.
claims.match_notes: The match is strong but remains below confirmed because no inspected source directly links the biographical record to an OSS personnel file.

claims.claim_text: In 1918, Edgar Salinger assisted Japanese-language translation work associated with the Naval Secret Service, Information Office.
claims.evidence_excerpt: translated, with a New Yorker who read and spoke Japanese, Edgar Salinger
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Jacob Viner recalled working with Salinger to translate Japanese mail material in 1918.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the rare exact name, New York context, Japanese-language skill and a second 1940 archival appearance.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely pre-OSS but too early to be treated as the immediate predecessor affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The role is published with qualification and is not labeled employment or immediate pre-OSS.

claims.claim_text: Edgar Salinger was listed as a sponsor of New York's Good Neighbor Committee in November 1940.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The committee's November 1940 circular prints Salinger's exact name in its sponsor list.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the rare exact name and corroborating New York Japanese-language record.
claims.temporal_assessment: A documented 1940 civic affiliation; it is neither an employer nor proven immediate to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The committee role is preserved as a professional affiliation and not converted to employment.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Richard G. Salomon is confirmed as the German-born historian whose archival collection contains material relating to his OSS employment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Leo Baeck Institute catalog explicitly identifies Richard G. Salomon's OSS employment records, while the MGH chronology identifies his concurrent Ohio professorships.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact full name, direct institutional archival description of OSS employment and aligned scholarly employment chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The professorships began in 1939, before OSS, but the precise OSS accession and leave chronology remains unreviewed.
claims.match_notes: Direct collection-level OSS evidence resolves the index identity; Box 673 and AR 3862 remain necessary for immediacy.

claims.claim_text: Richard G. Salomon was professor of medieval history at Kenyon College from 1939 to 1962.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional chronology dates Salomon's Kenyon College professorship from 1939 through 1962.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed index identity from the Leo Baeck Institute OSS collection description and matching MGH biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Employment began before OSS and continued afterward; no uninterrupted-service or immediate-predecessor inference is made.
claims.match_notes: The claim is documented prewar employment, not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Richard G. Salomon was professor of church history at Bexley Hall Seminary from 1939 to 1961.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional chronology dates Salomon's Bexley Hall Seminary professorship from 1939 through 1961.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed index identity from the Leo Baeck Institute OSS collection description and matching MGH biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Employment began before OSS and continued afterward; concurrent Kenyon employment prevents an immediate-predecessor designation.
claims.match_notes: Bexley Hall remains a separate organization rather than being silently merged into Kenyon College.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Robert A. Saltzstein is confirmed as the Milwaukee-born Detachment 101 veteran identified in an official Senate report as an OSS associate.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An official 1948 report names Robert Saltzstein of Milwaukee as an OSS associate; the obituary supplies the matching middle initial, hometown and Detachment 101 service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed from exact full name plus matching Milwaukee and OSS evidence across an official report and independent obituary.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both sources establish wartime OSS identity but do not identify a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: Postwar legal work is excluded from the pre-OSS employment fields.
